workflow.title: Route new website leads to Marcus or Priya and log assignments
workflow.goal: Route each new website lead that is not yet in lead-log: companies over 200 employees go to Priya; otherwise leads in California go to Marcus; all others go to Priya. Record every new assignment in the lead-log sheet so re-runs never log the same lead twice.

assumptions: Only leads with status 'new' are routed; contacted and spam leads are skipped.
Leads whose email already appears in lead-log are skipped, so re-runs do not duplicate assignments.
California is matched when region or country contains 'california', or region/country equals 'CA' (case-insensitive).
Assignment means recording the owner in lead-log; no e-mail or chat is sent.
companySize is a number of employees; a lead with company size over 200 goes to Priya even if in California.
The lead-log sheet already exists; if it is missing the run stops at the read step rather than logging blindly.
risks: assignedAt is not filled per row because no capability can stamp a per-row timestamp; the lead-log row has no assignment time.
A lead with a missing or non-numeric companySize will not match the size rule and falls through to the California or default rule.
Leads whose region or country is spelled differently (for example 'Calif.') will not be recognised as California.
Duplicate detection is by email; two different leads sharing one email in the same run are both logged once each only if neither was logged before.
successCriteria: Every new lead not already in lead-log appears in lead-log exactly once with the assignee chosen by the rules.
Leads already in lead-log are not appended again.
The appended row count matches the number of newly routed leads.
sheet.audit confirms the appended lead-log rows are present.

nodes.description: Read all rows of the leads sheet.
Keep only leads with status new.
Read the existing lead-log rows so already-assigned leads are not logged again.
Keep only new leads whose email is not already in lead-log.
Label each unlogged new lead: size over 200 goes to Priya; California goes to Marcus; everyone else goes to Priya.
Build lead-log rows with name, email, company and assignee.
Append the new assignments to the lead-log sheet.
Independently confirm the appended lead-log rows are in the sheet.

metadata.rationale: Ordered rules make the size rule win over the California rule. Leads already present in lead-log (matched by email) are excluded first so repeated runs do not duplicate assignments. Assignments are only logged, not messaged.
